land.text: Asmaka on the Godavari with Mulaka; infobox 'Succeeded by: Magadha'

successors.note: The page gives '425 or 345 BCE' for the end and names Magadha without a dynasty; the Cliopatria row alive in -345 is the Shaishunaga dynasty (-404..-334). The Mahajanapadas page has 'The Nandas usurped the throne of Shishunaga dynasty c. 345 BCE', so the Nanda Empire (Cliopatria from -333) is the alternative.

capitals.name: Potali (Podana; Bodhan)
capitals.note: 'Capital: Potali, also called Podana, Paudanyapura, or Potana'; 'Most scholars identify it with present-day Bodhan in Telangana'. Coordinates are Bodhan's.

correction.text: Asmaka 'located on the Godavari river', identified with 'modern Nizamabad district', with its capital Potali at Bodhan

keyframe_review.note: The 5,467 km2 shape (centroid 78.28E 19.83N) lies in Adilabad north of the Godavari, 130 km from Bodhan; the page puts Asmaka 'on the Godavari river' in 'modern Nizamabad district', and the Mahajanapadas page has 'The river Godavari separated the country of the Assakas from that of the Mulakas', so the core is moved to the Nizamabad-Bodhan reach of the river (about 15,000 km2). The infobox gives no area.

correction.text: Asmaka on the Godavari with Mulaka, 'the small kingdom located to its west' across the river, annexed 'during the Mahajanapada period'

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 56 km2 change at -550 has no event on the pages; the keyframe date is used instead for the undated annexation of Mulaka to the west (ledger -550, confidence 1), so the corrected shape adds the Mulakas' country across the Godavari.

correction.text: unchanged from -550, holding to -346 rather than -351: the page ends Asmaka in '425 or 345 BCE according to the Buddhist texts and Puranas' and the later date is drawn

keyframe_review.note: If the 425 BCE date is the right one, this shape and the last eighty years of the previous one belong to Magadha; the Cliopatria keyframe at -366 has no event of its own.

region.text: Asmaka 'located on the Godavari river', identified with 'modern Nizamabad district', with its capital Potali at Bodhan

ledger.note: c. 600 BCE: Asmaka, the only Mahajanapada of the Deccan, is ruled from Potali on the Godavari. 'Ashmaka (or Assaka) was the only Mahajanapada located in South India'; infobox 'c. 700 BCE' established, 'Capital: Potali, also called Podana, Paudanyapura, or Potana', 'Most scholars identify it with present-day Bodhan in Telangana'. -600 is the Mahajanapada convention; the infobox's c. 700 BCE is not drawn.

region.text: Mulaka, 'the small kingdom located to its west', the Mulakas' country across the Godavari

ledger.note: Mid-6th century BCE (undated): Asmaka annexes Mulaka to its west. 'Asmaka annexed the small kingdom of Mulaka located to its west during the Mahajanapada period'; it thereby 'became the southern neighbour of the kingdom of Avanti'; Mahajanapadas page: 'At one time, Assaka included Mulaka and abutted Avanti'. The year is Cliopatria's -550 shape change; the region is an 80 km radius on the Godavari at Nanded, west of Nizamabad (the Mulaka page would not load). Mulaka needs a dossier.

region.text: Asmaka on the Godavari with Mulaka, 'the small kingdom located to its west' across the river, annexed 'during the Mahajanapada period'

ledger.note: c. 345 BCE: Asmaka passes to Magadha. Infobox 'Disestablished 425 or 345 BCE', 'Succeeded by: Magadha'; the page names no conqueror and no campaign. The Cliopatria row alive in -345 is the Shaishunaga dynasty (-404..-334); the Mahajanapadas page has 'The Nandas usurped the throne of Shishunaga dynasty c. 345 BCE', so the Nanda Empire is the other candidate. Cliopatria ends the row in -351.

wars.name: Kalinga's invasion of Assaka
wars.outcome: In a Jataka tale the Kalinga king invaded Assaka and was defeated through diplomacy; he 'was forced to send a portion of his daughters' dowry to Assaka' and the two kings kept peaceful relations. No land changed hands.
wars.note: Undated; the years are the state's span. Kalinga of this period has no Cliopatria row (the Kalinga row is -318..-171).

wars.name: Asmaka's annexation of Mulaka

zones.text: Mulaka, 'the small kingdom located to its west', the Mulakas' country across the Godavari

wars.outcome: Mulaka annexed by Asmaka 'during the Mahajanapada period'; Asmaka 'became the southern neighbour of the kingdom of Avanti'.
wars.note: Undated; the ledger places the annexation at Cliopatria's -550 shape change.

certainty.note: The Godavari is the only line the pages give (it 'separated the country of the Assakas from that of the Mulakas' before the annexation); every other edge is a radius.

sources.title: Asmaka
sources.note: Identity, infobox (c. 700 BCE to 425 or 345 BCE, Potali/Bodhan, succeeded by Magadha), the Godavari location, the annexation of Mulaka, the Kalinga Jataka.

sources.title: Mahajanapadas
sources.note: Overview of the sixteen states ('from the sixth to fourth centuries BCE'), the Mahajanapada convention behind every -600 start, and the per-state location notes; shared by the five janapada dossiers of batch sa-01-a.

notes: Cliopatria's three near-identical shapes sit north of the Godavari in Adilabad; the page places Asmaka on the river in Nizamabad district with Potali at Bodhan, so all three are moved (adjust). The only dated facts are the Mahajanapada convention and the infobox's '425 or 345 BCE' end; -345 is drawn. Unsettled: the Mulaka annexation is undated (placed at Cliopatria's -550 keyframe, confidence 1) and the Mulaka page would not load under 'Mulaka' or 'Mūlaka'; who took Asmaka (Shaishunaga or Nanda) and when (425 or 345); Kalinga of the 6th century has no row. Gazetteer: Nizamabad and Nanded are present; Bodhan (18.67N 77.90E) is not and is given as coordinates in capitals only.
